# CloudThinker

> CloudThinker is an Autonomous Cloud Operations (AgenticOps) platform where specialized AI agents manage infrastructure, review code, resolve incidents, and optimize costs across AWS, Azure, GCP, and Kubernetes. Modules: Code Review, Deep Response Engine, CostOps, SecOps, ChatOps, and Skills.

## Get started — Start here

- [CloudThinker](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/index.md): Meet the AI agents that manage infrastructure, review code, resolve incidents, and optimize costs across AWS, Azure, GCP, and Kubernetes.
- [Quick Start](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/quickstart.md): Register, connect AWS, verify the connection, and run your first AI-powered cost analysis — with a clear success state for every step.
- [First Prompts by Role](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/tutorial/agenticops.md): Find your role, copy a prompt, and get a real result from your own cloud environment in about 10 minutes.

## Get started — Core concepts

- [AI Agents](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/agents.md): Meet the five specialized CloudThinker agents and choose the right one for cost, security, database, and Kubernetes work
- [CloudThinker Language](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/language.md): Look up the @agent #tool syntax: agent mentions, tool tags, context modifiers, and prompt patterns for every agent
- [Capabilities](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/capabilities.md): Look up every tool tag agents accept and the output each one produces — dashboards, reports, recommendations, and alerts.
- [Operations Hub](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/operations-hub.md): Browse and run pre-built cloud operations across cost, security, performance, and Kubernetes categories.

## Features — Code Review

- [AI Code Review](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/overview.md): Catch bugs, security vulnerabilities, and quality issues on every pull request with context-aware AI reviews
- [Code Review Setup](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/setup.md): Connect your GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps repositories for automated AI-powered code reviews
- [Mention Commands](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/mention-commands.md): Interact with CloudThinker directly from MR/PR comments
- [Convention Rules](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/convention-rules.md): Guide the AI reviewer with your team's coding conventions, both the convention files already in your repository and rules CloudThinker learns automatically from past reviews.
- [Leaderboard](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/leaderboard.md): Understand the Developer Leaderboard scoring formula that balances code quality with productivity.
- [Code Review Analytics](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/analytics.md): Explore PR volume, quality scores, finding distributions, and per-developer performance across all reviewed repositories
- [Skill Matrix](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/skill-matrix.md): Visualize developer proficiency across code review domains with heatmap and radar charts that map strengths and surface growth areas.
- [Extensions](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/code-review/extensions.md): Enrich code reviews with context from issue trackers

## Features — CostOps

- [CostOps](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/overview.md): Find, prioritize, and track cloud cost savings across AWS, GCP, and Azure with AI-generated recommendations
- [Recommendations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/recommendations.md): Look up recommendation attributes, sources, and categories, and move savings opportunities from finding to implemented change
- [Cost Analytics](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/analytics.md): Explore cloud spending trends, attribution, anomalies, and forecasts across AWS, GCP, and Azure
- [Savings Tracking](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cost-optimization/savings.md): Measure realized cloud cost savings against projections and track optimization ROI over time
- [Keepers](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/infrastructure/cloudkeepers.md): Enable autonomous keepers that catch cost, security, and performance drift and turn findings into tracked recommendations.

## Features — Deep Response Engine

- [Deep Response Engine](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/overview.md): Learn how CloudThinker turns raw cloud signals into investigated, remediated incidents through the Pulse and Incident stages.
- [How Pulse Works](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/pulse/overview.md): Learn how Pulse turns raw monitoring events into ranked clusters through an eight-stage pipeline of dedup, suppression, and AI triage
- [Clusters & Suppression](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/pulse/clusters.md): Understand how Pulse groups signals into clusters and cuts noise through seven automatic suppression layers.
- [Pulse Setup](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/pulse/setup.md): Wire AWS pollers, chat channels, and monitoring webhooks into Pulse so actionable clusters escalate to incidents
- [Pulse Analytics](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/pulse/analytics.md): Measure signal volume, noise reduction, cluster resolution time, and source conversion rates over time
- [Root Cause Analysis](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/root-cause-analysis.md): Understand how CloudThinker agents investigate incidents with hypothesis tracking, evidence chains, and confidence scoring
- [Manual Incident Logging](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/manual-logging.md): Create incidents manually when automated alerting isn't configured or immediate investigation is needed
- [Incident Webhook Integrations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/webhook-integrations/overview.md): Connect your alerting platforms to automatically create incidents with AI-powered investigation
- [AWS CloudWatch](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/webhook-integrations/cloudwatch.md): Set up AWS CloudWatch alarms to automatically create incidents in CloudThinker via Amazon EventBridge
- [Runbooks](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/runbooks.md): Connect your team's operational runbooks so AI agents can find and execute remediation steps during incidents
- [Incident Memory](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/incident/incident-memory.md): Speed up incident investigations using AI that learns from past resolutions to find root causes faster.

## Features — SecOps

- [App Pentesting](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/security/pentest.md): Register an app, attach logins and source code, then run a scoped agentic pentest that returns findings with proof.

## Features — Infrastructure

- [Infrastructure Management](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/infrastructure/overview.md): Discover, map, assess, and act on every cloud resource across AWS, GCP, and Azure from one place
- [Resources](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/infrastructure/resources.md): Discover cloud assets across accounts, scope scans by tags, and act on cost, security, and performance findings from one inventory.
- [Topology](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/infrastructure/topology.md): Map cloud infrastructure dependencies visually and trace incidents back to their root cause with the Topology Explorer
- [Plan](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/infrastructure/plan.md): Save findings as recommendations, capture approvals, and schedule execution from one shared backlog.
- [Infrastructure Assessment](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/infrastructure/assessment.md): Run automated Well-Architected assessments on discovered resources and turn findings into a remediation plan.
- [Infrastructure Analytics](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/infrastructure/analytics.md): Monitor infrastructure utilization, performance, and reliability trends across connected cloud environments

## Features — ChatOps

- [Slack Integration](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/slack-integration.md): Run CloudThinker AI operations directly from Slack — manage infrastructure, review costs, and investigate incidents without leaving your workspace
- [Microsoft Teams Integration](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/teams-integration.md): Run cloud operations from Microsoft Teams by interacting with CloudThinker agents, receiving Adaptive Card alerts, and coordinating incidents.

## Features — Skills

- [Skills](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/skills/overview.md): Extend AI agents with domain-specific knowledge, custom workflows, and organization-specific procedures
- [Custom Skills](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/skills/custom-skills.md): Create, enable, and assign workspace skills that encode your team's knowledge for agents to apply on every task
- [Skill Format](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/skills/skill-format.md): Write SKILL.md files agents follow reliably — file structure, frontmatter fields, and instruction patterns

## Features — Artifacts & Dashboards

- [Artifacts](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/artifacts/overview.md): Generate comprehensive reports, build custom dashboards, and export data for analysis

## Administration — Organization

- [Organizations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/organization.md): Manage your CloudThinker organization settings, members, and billing
- [Workspaces](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/workspaces.md): Create workspaces to isolate agents, connections, and knowledge for each team, project, or environment
- [Workspace Members](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/workspace-users.md): Manage member access and roles within your CloudThinker workspace
- [Workspace Branding](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/workspace-branding.md): Apply your company logo, name, and chart color palette to artifact PDF exports and in-app charts

## Administration — Agents

- [Alex](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/agents/alex.md): Analyze cloud costs, right-size resources, and optimize multi-cloud infrastructure across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
- [Oliver](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/agents/oliver.md): Audit security posture, detect vulnerabilities, and generate compliance evidence across cloud environments.
- [Tony](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/agents/tony.md): Optimize database queries, tune performance, and analyze data across SQL and NoSQL platforms with Tony.
- [Kai](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/agents/kai.md): Manage Kubernetes clusters, optimize container workloads, and troubleshoot EKS, GKE, and AKS with Kai.
- [Anna](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/agents/anna.md): Coordinate multi-agent operations, manage complex cloud projects, and produce executive reports with Anna.
- [Customize Agents](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/agents/customize.md): Edit how default agents talk, choose what they can reach, and create your own agents
- [Agent Configuration](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/configuration.md): Scope each agent's builtin tools, connections, and custom instructions from the Agents page

## Administration — Automation & Autonomy

- [Autonomous Operations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/automation/autonomous-agents.md): Learn what CloudThinker runs on its own — keepers, scheduled tasks, Pulse triage — and how Manual and Auto modes keep you in control
- [Tasks & Scheduling](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/automation/tasks.md): Schedule agent prompts to run daily, weekly, or monthly, and manage every automated task in your workspace
- [Approval](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/approval.md): Control when agents pause for approval by setting each tool to auto-approve, require approval, or disabled
- [Auto Mode](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/auto-mode.md): Let AI approve agent actions automatically so chats flow without click-by-click approval

## Administration — Connections

- [Connections](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/overview.md): Connect your cloud providers, databases, and services to CloudThinker for unified AI-powered operations
- [AWS](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/aws.md): Connect AWS to CloudThinker for cost analysis, security auditing, and infrastructure management via IAM role or access keys
- [Google Cloud](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/gcp.md): Connect Google Cloud to CloudThinker for resource management, cost optimization, and security monitoring via service account
- [Azure](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/azure.md): Connect Microsoft Azure to CloudThinker for multi-cloud operations, cost analysis, and compliance monitoring
- [Firebase](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/firebase.md): Connect Firebase to CloudThinker for project and app inventory, SDK config lookup, and Firestore/Storage security-rule audits
- [Cloudflare](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/cloudflare.md): Connect Cloudflare to CloudThinker for DNS management, CDN optimization, and security configuration
- [Vercel](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/vercel.md): Connect Vercel to CloudThinker for project inventory, deployment inspection, runtime log triage, and domain auditing
- [Kubernetes](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/kubernetes.md): Connect Kubernetes clusters to CloudThinker for workload analysis, resource optimization, and cluster operations
- [SSH](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/ssh.md): Connect your own servers to CloudThinker over SSH so agents can run shell commands using key-based authentication and trusted host keys
- [HashiCorp Vault](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/vault.md): Connect HashiCorp Vault to read KV secrets, issue dynamic credentials, and audit policies, tokens, and health via Token or AppRole auth
- [Keycloak](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/keycloak.md): Connect Keycloak to CloudThinker for identity and access management operations
- [PostgreSQL](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/postgresql.md): Connect PostgreSQL databases to CloudThinker for query analysis, index optimization, and performance monitoring
- [MySQL](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/mysql.md): Connect MySQL databases to CloudThinker for query analysis, performance monitoring, and database optimization
- [MongoDB](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/mongodb.md): Connect MongoDB databases to CloudThinker for document query analysis, performance tuning, and operational insights
- [Redis](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/redis.md): Connect Redis to CloudThinker for cache performance monitoring across self-hosted, Upstash, or Redis Cloud deployments
- [Neon](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/neon.md): Connect Neon Postgres to CloudThinker with OAuth-powered MCP for project discovery, schema inspection, and database operations
- [Elasticsearch](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/elasticsearch.md): Connect Elasticsearch to CloudThinker for log analysis, index management, and search performance optimization
- [Kafka](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/kafka.md): Connect Apache Kafka on Confluent Cloud to CloudThinker with scope-based credentials for stream monitoring and management
- [RabbitMQ](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/rabbitmq.md): Connect RabbitMQ to CloudThinker via the Management HTTP API for queue depth, consumer lag, DLQ analysis, cluster and node health, and alarm monitoring
- [Flespi](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/flespi.md): Connect Flespi IoT telematics to CloudThinker for GPS device management, fleet telemetry, and IoT data analysis
- [Grafana](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/grafana.md): Connect Grafana to CloudThinker for dashboard integration, metric analysis, and unified observability
- [Prometheus](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/prometheus.md): Connect Prometheus, Thanos, VictoriaMetrics, or Grafana Cloud for read-only PromQL queries, metric discovery, target health, and alert inspection
- [Datadog](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/datadog.md): Connect Datadog to CloudThinker for log search, metric queries, infrastructure monitoring, and incident investigation
- [New Relic](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/newrelic.md): Connect New Relic to CloudThinker for APM, infrastructure monitoring, NRQL queries, alerting, and incident investigation via the New Relic MCP server
- [Dynatrace](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/dynatrace.md): Connect Dynatrace to CloudThinker for DQL queries, problem investigation, security vulnerability review, and entity discovery
- [AppDynamics](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/appdynamics.md): Connect AppDynamics (Cisco) APM to CloudThinker for application health monitoring, health-rule violation triage, and metric review
- [Coralogix](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/coralogix.md): Connect Coralogix to CloudThinker for log search, metrics, traces, incident triage, and pipeline health investigation
- [SigNoz](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/signoz.md): Connect SigNoz to CloudThinker to investigate service latency, search logs, audit alert rules, and drill into distributed traces across your stack
- [Zabbix](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/zabbix.md): Connect Zabbix monitoring to CloudThinker for infrastructure monitoring, alerting, and performance analysis
- [Better Stack](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/betterstack.md): Connect Better Stack to CloudThinker for uptime monitoring, incident triage, on-call visibility, and log search across your observability stack
- [Rollbar](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/rollbar.md): Connect Rollbar to CloudThinker for error triage, top-error tracking, and deployment-correlated investigation
- [Langfuse](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/langfuse.md): Connect Langfuse to CloudThinker for LLM trace investigation, conversation debugging, evaluation review, and prompt auditing
- [Jenkins](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/jenkins.md): Connect Jenkins CI/CD server to CloudThinker for build pipeline monitoring, job analysis, and deployment tracking
- [CircleCI](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/circleci.md): Connect CircleCI to CloudThinker for pipeline status monitoring, workflow and job analysis, build log triage, and approval-gated pipeline controls
- [ArgoCD](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/argocd.md): Connect ArgoCD to CloudThinker for GitOps operations and application management
- [AWX](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/awx.md): Connect Ansible AWX to CloudThinker to launch job templates, monitor jobs, manage inventories, and orchestrate automation workflows
- [SonarQube](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/sonarqube.md): Connect SonarQube to CloudThinker for continuous code quality analysis, security scanning, and technical debt tracking
- [GitGuardian](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/gitguardian.md): Connect GitGuardian to CloudThinker for secrets detection, incident investigation, and honeytoken monitoring across your code
- [PagerDuty](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/pagerduty.md): Connect PagerDuty to CloudThinker for on-call management, incident alerting, and escalation policy integration
- [ServiceNow](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/servicenow.md): Connect ServiceNow ITSM to CloudThinker for incident, change request, problem, and CMDB management
- [Atlassian](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/atlassian.md): Connect Atlassian Jira and Confluence to CloudThinker for issue tracking, knowledge base, and project management
- [Jira Service Management](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/jsm.md): Connect Jira Service Management Operations for alert triage, on-call visibility, and incident sync during response
- [Backlog](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/backlog.md): Connect Backlog by Nulab to CloudThinker for issue tracking, milestone planning, wiki, and pull-request context
- [MCP](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/connections/mcp.md): Connect custom tools and APIs to CloudThinker via Model Context Protocol (MCP) for extensible agent capabilities

- [Usage](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/billing/usage.md): Track daily, bonus, and premium credit consumption and configure Pay-As-You-Go top-up to keep agent operations running.

## Developer — APIs & Tooling

- [API](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/api/overview.md): Access CloudThinker programmatically to manage workspaces, agents, recommendations, and incidents via authenticated HTTPS endpoints
- [MCP Server](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/mcp/overview.md): Expose CloudThinker's cloud-ops tools and data to external MCP-compatible AI clients like Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Windsurf
- [CLI](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/cli/overview.md): Run CloudThinker agent conversations, query resources, and manage operations directly from your terminal
- [Webhooks](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/webhooks/overview.md): Send CloudThinker events to external systems with configurable webhooks

## Developer — Deployment

- [Deployment](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/deployment/overview.md): Deploy CloudThinker in self-hosted, dedicated, or air-gapped environments for regulated and data-residency-constrained use cases

## Resources — Learn

- [Introduction](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/introduction.md): The CloudThinker Field Guide to AgenticOps — why this book exists, the whole argument in one page, and the reading map for the ten chapters that follow.
- [Chapter 1 · The Operations Complexity Crisis](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-1-complexity-crisis.md): Modern infrastructure has outgrown human cognitive capacity. The math no longer works.
- [Chapter 2 · From Automation to Autonomy](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-2-automation-to-autonomy.md): Agentic operations is the fourth generation of a forty-year evolution. Understanding the lineage explains both its power and its prerequisites.
- [Chapter 3 · What Agentic Infrastructure Operations Actually Is](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-3-what-is-aio.md): Definitions matter, because 'agent' is the most abused word in enterprise software. The working definition, the L0–L4 autonomy spectrum, the five-question vendor test, and what's actually in scope today.
- [Chapter 4 · Architecture: Multi-Agent Systems for Operations](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-4-architecture.md): The reference architecture that production deployments are converging on: an orchestrator, a team of specialists, a closed operational loop, and a context layer that makes them smart.
- [Chapter 5 · The Agent Team: Roles and Responsibilities](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-5-agent-team.md): Designing an agent organization is organizational design. The roster, the work flow, the agent-to-human interface, and four production case studies.
- [Chapter 6 · Trust, Guardrails, and Governance](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-6-trust-governance.md): Autonomy is earned, not configured. Governance is not the brake on agentic operations — it is the enabler. The five-level guardrail stack, the deployment-model dial, the FSI lens, and the agent-layer threat model.
- [Chapter 7 · Humans on the Loop: The New Operating Model](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-7-humans-on-the-loop.md): Agentic operations is a people transformation wearing a technology costume. From executor to supervisor, how roles change, and the trust ladder.
- [Chapter 8 · Measuring What Matters](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-8-measuring.md): Agentic operations succeeds or fails on evidence. The eight-KPI dashboard, ROI math, unit economics, and the evaluation harness.
- [Chapter 9 · The Implementation Roadmap](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-9-roadmap.md): A staged, evidence-driven adoption path: ninety days to first value, twelve months to a new operating model. Five readiness foundations, the 90-day pilot, scaling, and the five ways canceled projects die.
- [Chapter 10 · The Road Ahead](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/chapter-10-road-ahead.md): Where agentic infrastructure operations goes from here — five near-term trajectories, the strategic window, and the hyperscaler-vs-unified architectural choice.
- [About CloudThinker](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio/about-cloudthinker.md): The unified multi-cloud agentic operations platform — engineers on the loop, not in the loop.
- [Introduction · Engineer Edition](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/introduction.md): The engineering manual for earning autonomy — the executive summary, the eight challenges, and the reading map for the engineers who will evaluate, integrate, and defend an agentic operations platform.
- [Chapter 1 · The Anatomy of an Operations Agent](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-1-agent-anatomy.md): Everything that matters — quality, cost, safety — is decided by what you put inside the agent loop.
- [Chapter 2 · Context Engineering: The Real Determinant of Agent Quality](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-2-context-engineering.md): Two agents on the same model, tools, and incident can differ by an order of magnitude in usefulness. The difference is context.
- [Chapter 3 · Tools, Skills, and the Protocol Layer](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-3-tools-skills-protocol.md): Tools are where reasoning touches the world. Their design decides more about safety and reliability than any prompt.
- [Chapter 4 · Orchestration and Two-Engine Economics](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-4-orchestration-economics.md): Multi-agent is not a philosophy; it is a set of engineering trade-offs about context, credentials, latency, and cost.
- [Chapter 5 · The Threat Model: Your Agent Is an Attack Surface](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-5-threat-model.md): An operations agent executes reasoning derived from whatever it reads — and it reads everything.
- [Chapter 6 · Policy, Approvals, and Execution Safety as Code](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-6-policy-approvals.md): The trust ladder is a promise to your organization. Policy-as-code is how the promise is kept when nobody is watching.
- [Chapter 7 · Evaluating Agents Like Production Systems](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-7-evaluating-agents.md): The benchmark numbers are humbling, the benchmarks are gameable, and your environment is the only test that matters.
- [Chapter 8 · Observing the Observer](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-8-observing-the-observer.md): The agent fleet is a production service — one whose failures are decisions, not exceptions.
- [Chapter 9 · AgentOps: Running the Fleet on Day 2](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-9-agentops-day-2.md): The pilot ends; the fleet remains: version management, model migrations, memory hygiene, and postmortems for a new kind of teammate.
- [Chapter 10 · The Vertical Pillars: Complexity, Cost, and Security & Compliance](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-10-vertical-pillars.md): One harness, three verticals — the machinery of Parts 01–03 creates value only when it is pointed at a domain, and each domain bends the engineering differently.
- [Chapter 11 · The Failure Catalog — and Build vs. Buy for Engineers](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-11-failure-catalog.md): Twelve production failure modes, each with its detection signal and its antidote — then the build-vs-buy question answered the way engineers actually face it.
- [Chapter 12 · The Future of Cloud Operations: The Autonomous Mission Loop](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/chapter-12-autonomous-mission-loop.md): A fleet of narrow, standing missions that trigger themselves, verify their own work, and run under policy — while engineers move from the loop to above it.
- [Appendix A · The POC Test Plan](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/appendix-a-poc-test-plan.md): A two-to-four-week evaluation protocol with signed pass/fail gates for testing any agentic operations platform against your own incidents.
- [Appendix B · The Agent Platform Engineering Checklist](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/appendix-b-engineering-checklist.md): Forty scored items across eight surfaces for grading a vendor platform or reviewing an internal agent build.
- [Appendix C · Glossary — Engineer Delta](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/appendix-c-glossary.md): Engineering terms that extend the Field Guide glossary — from steps and trajectories to taint tagging and kill switches.
- [Appendix D · Sources and How to Read the Numbers](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/appendix-d-sources.md): The primary sources behind this edition's figures, with the rules for weighing benchmark, vendor, and analyst numbers.
- [About CloudThinker · Engineer Edition](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/aio-engineer/about-cloudthinker.md): The unified multi-cloud agentic operations platform — engineers on the loop, not in the loop. The harness this book describes, as one platform.
- [FAQ](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/learn/faq.md): Find answers to common questions about CloudThinker, AI agents, pricing, security, and cloud operations

## Resources — Scenarios

- [Kubernetes Health Monitoring](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/use-cases/kubernetes-health-monitoring.md): Use Kai to monitor EKS cluster health, surface resource waste, and get HPA recommendations before problems reach production.
- [Operating Multi-AWS Accounts](https://docs.cloudthinker.io/guide/use-cases/multi-aws-accounts.md): Operate multiple AWS accounts from one workspace using IAM AssumeRole shortcuts to switch account context on demand
